extraction.name: TOFU: Task of Fictitious Unlearning
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating entity-level unlearning in large language models, comprising 200 fictitious author profiles with 20 question-answer pairs per author. It provides forget/retain splits targeting 2, 10, or 20 authors and evaluates both forget quality and model utility.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, and J. Zico Kolter
extraction.citeAs: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, and J. Zico Kolter. TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. arXiv:2401.06121v1, 11 January 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors synthesized fictitious author biographies using GPT-4. They prompted GPT-4 with predefined attributes including birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards, parents' professions, and book-title seeds, requesting 20 detailed, self-contained question-answer pairs per author. Book-title seeds were created by randomly selecting keywords from two books from each genre in the Goodreads Books dataset on Kaggle. An initial 50-author dataset generated with a generic prompt was inspected for repetitive patterns; the final generation strategy deterministically seeded attributes to increase diversity and reduce confounding information from GPT-4's pretraining data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The author biographies and question-answer pairs were generated by GPT-4 and are entirely fictitious. Predefined author attributes served as seed data. Keywords for generated book titles were sourced from the Goodreads Books dataset on Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jealousleopard/goodreadsbooks.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was divided into retain/forget splits of 90/10, 95/5, and 99/1 percent, corresponding to forgetting 20, 10, or 2 authors. For evaluation, GPT-4 generated a paraphrased version of each answer and five factually incorrect perturbations that preserved the general textual template. In the preference-optimization baseline, forget-set answers were replaced with alternatives such as 'I do not know the answer,' using 100 response variants.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The generation prompt required question-answer pairs in a strict 'Q: ...? A: ... .' format, with detailed, self-contained answers and the author's full name in each question.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: GPT-4 generated the questions and their corresponding answers from seeded fictitious author attributes. These generated answers served as ground truth. GPT-4 also generated paraphrased correct answers and five factually incorrect answer perturbations for truth-ratio evaluation.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The synthetic profiles contain names, birthplaces, gender, birth years, gender orientation, and parents' occupations, alongside literary and biographical information. The paper explicitly states that the author biographies are entirely fabricated rather than information about real individuals.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to support methods that protect privacy by removing information from trained language models and to simulate Right to be Forgotten requests concerning private individuals rarely mentioned in training data. The authors aim to improve evaluation of unlearning and help develop more secure, trustworthy AI systems whose privacy protections support safe and legally compliant deployment.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: An initial 50-author dataset generated without seeded attributes showed concentrated birth years between 1970 and 1980, especially August and 1975; repeated book-title words such as 'echoes,' 'shadows,' 'tides,' and 'whispers'; mostly fictional books and no self-help books; and similar university-educated upbringings and 'magical' writing styles. The authors identified a risk that GPT-4's pretraining biases could leak into synthetic biographies. They mitigated this through deterministic attribute seeding and diverse book-title keywords, reporting greater diversity based on manual inspection.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: TOFU covers entity-level forgetting, not instance-level forgetting, behavior-level unlearning or alignment, or in-context unlearning. It studies information learned during finetuning rather than pretraining. Exact forget and retain sets are supplied, so it does not address the real-world difficulty of identifying these sets. Forget quality is an empirical approximation of indistinguishability rather than a verification of formal approximate unlearning; models generating gibberish may achieve high forget-quality scores, making joint evaluation with model utility necessary. The benchmark constrains unlearning compute to scale linearly with the number of forget samples, a choice the authors acknowledge may not be optimal.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Finetuning pretrained language models on fictitious author question-answer pairs; developing and benchmarking entity-level machine-unlearning algorithms; and evaluating forget quality alongside retained model utility. Models should forget the designated 1%, 5%, or 10% author subsets while retaining performance on the remaining synthetic authors, real-author questions, and world facts. Benchmark unlearning compute must scale linearly with the number of forget samples.
